question: The nineteenth century saw the golden age of Kathak under the patronage of Wajid Ali Shah, the last Nawab of __________.
solution:
The correct answer is **__Oudh.__**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The 19th century saw the golden age of Kathak under the patronage of Wajid Ali Shah, the last Nawab of Awadh.
 
• He established the **Lucknow** **Gharana** with its strong accent on bhava.
 
• Kathak grew into a major art form under the patronage of **Wajid Ali Shah**, the last Nawab of Awadh.
 
• The significant supporters of Kathak were **the Mughal rulers, their aristocrats, the courts of Rajasthan and Lucknow, and the last Nawab of Awadh - Wajid Ali Shah**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• The first name that comes with the mention of dance forms in Hyderabad is the **Kuchipudi**.
 
• Kuchipudi is a dance form that also uses some amount of acting which is accompanied by Carnatic music.
 
• Kathak is the principal dance of northern India and is widely practiced in **Uttar Pradesh(Rampur, Jaunpur), Rajasthan, Delhi, Madhya Pradesh**, and even parts of western and eastern India today.
